label: Sie
notes: The base rows: Sie with the third-person plural verb, as to any adult stranger.

label: du
notes: du with the second-person singular verb and imperative, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller; ihr, its plural, where a question is put to a whole shop, restaurant or house (Habt ihr einen Tisch frei?). e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: vous
notes: The base rows: vous with the second-person plural verb, as to any adult stranger.

label: tu
notes: tu with the second-person singular verb and imperative and s'il te plaît, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller; a question put to a whole shop or restaurant keeps vous, which is the plural of tu too. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: usted
notes: The base rows: usted with the third-person singular verb, as to any adult stranger.

label: tú
notes: tú with the second-person singular verb and imperative, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller (tuteo; regional vos is not written). The plural stays ustedes, which is the familiar plural too in the Latin-American Spanish of these rows. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: вы
notes: The base rows: вы with the second-person plural verb, as to any adult stranger.

label: ты
notes: ты with the second-person singular verb and imperative, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller. A ты past tense or short adjective agrees with the listener's gender, which this axis does not ask, so such sentences keep their base row or take an ungendered wording. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: 해요
notes: The base rows: 해요체 (합쇼체 in set phrases such as 감사합니다), with the honorific -시- toward the listener, as to any adult stranger.

label: 해
notes: 해체 (반말): the -요 dropped, and the honorific -시- with it, to a child or a friend of one's own age. Korean marks the hearer in every sentence ending, so this covers sentences about the speaker too. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: Lei
notes: The base rows: Lei with the third-person singular verb, and the subjunctive for a request (Si fermi, Mi dica), as to any adult stranger.

label: tu
notes: tu with the second-person singular verb and imperative (Fermati, Dimmi, Non usare), to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller; a question put to a whole shop, restaurant or hotel keeps voi (Avete...?), which is the plural of tu too. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: você
notes: The base rows: the third-person singular verb with the pronoun left out, as one addresses o senhor, a senhora or você -- any adult stranger, in Portugal and in Brazil alike.

label: tu
notes: tu with the second-person singular verb and imperative (Para aqui, Diz-me, Não uses), the European familiar address, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller. The Brazilian text_alt is inherited unchanged, since in Brazil você with the third-person verb is itself the familiar address; a question put to a whole hotel keeps the plural (Têm...?, Podem...?), which is the same in both registers. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: です
notes: The base rows: 丁寧体 (です・ます体), the 丁寧語 です and ます closing every sentence, as to any adult stranger.

label: だ
notes: 普通体 (だ体): です becomes だ and ます the dictionary form, a question is asked with a rise and no か, ください becomes the bare て form, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller. Japanese marks the hearer in every sentence ending, so this covers sentences about the speaker too; the casual first person and the gendered sentence-final particles are left out. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: siz
notes: The base rows: siz with the second-person plural verb, imperative (-in, -yin) and possessive (-iniz), as to any adult stranger.

label: sen
notes: sen with the second-person singular verb, the bare-stem imperative and the singular possessive (-in), to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller; siz is also the plural of sen, so a question put to a whole hotel (Boş odanız var mı?) does not change. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: आप
notes: The base rows: आप with the plural verb and the -इए imperative (दीजिए, बोलिए), as to any adult stranger.

label: तुम
notes: तुम with the -ओ imperative (दो, बोलो) and तुम्हारा, तुम्हें, to a friend of one's own age, a child or a fellow traveller; तू, intimate or rude to a stranger, is never written. Only second-person forms change. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: آپ
notes: The base rows: آپ with the plural verb and the -یے imperative (دیجیے, بولیے), as to any adult stranger.

label: تم
notes: تم with the -و imperative (دو, بولو) and تمہارا, تمہیں, to a friend of one's own age, a child or a fellow traveller; تو, intimate or rude to a stranger, is never written. Only second-person forms change. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: Ви
notes: The base rows: Ви with the second-person plural verb and imperative (можете, говоріть, зупиніться), as to any adult stranger.

label: ти
notes: ти with the second-person singular verb and imperative (можеш, говори, зупинися), to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller; ви is also the plural of ти. A ти past tense or conditional agrees with the listener's gender, which this axis does not ask, so such sentences take an ungendered wording or keep their base row. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: pan/pani
notes: The base rows: the address-free polite request (Proszę + infinitive, Czy mogę prosić o ...?, Czy jest ...?), as to any adult stranger; the listener switch gives the pan / pani forms with the third-person verb.

label: ty
notes: ty with the second-person singular verb and imperative (możesz, mów, zatrzymaj się), and wy, its plural, for a question put to a whole restaurant (Co polecacie?), to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller. A ty past tense, conditional or adjective agrees with the listener (mógłbyś / mogłabyś, miły / miła): with the listener switch on those rows are combined with listener_gender, and off it the familiar row is the present, one form for both. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: vy
notes: The base rows: vykání, vy with the second-person plural verb and imperative (můžete, mluvte, zastavte), as to any adult stranger.

label: ty
notes: tykání, ty with the second-person singular verb and imperative (můžeš, mluv, zastav) and the greetings ahoj and čau, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller; vy is also the plural of ty, so a question put to a whole shop or hotel (Máte volné pokoje?) does not change. A conditional agrees with the listener (mohl bys / mohla bys): with the listener switch on those rows are combined with listener_gender, and off it the familiar row is the present můžeš, one form for both. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: u
notes: The base rows: u with its verb (kunt u, heeft u, stopt u), uw, and alstublieft, as to any adult stranger.

label: jij
notes: jij, written as the unstressed je the sentences call for, with its verb (kun je, heb je, stop), the possessive je, and alsjeblieft, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller; jullie, its plural, where a question is put to a whole shop (Hebben jullie dit op voorraad?). e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: εσείς
notes: The base rows: εσείς, the plural of politeness, with the second-person plural verb and imperative (μπορείτε, σταματήστε) and σας, as to any adult stranger.

label: εσύ
notes: εσύ with the second-person singular verb and imperative (μπορείς, σταμάτα, πες) and σου, and γεια σου, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller; εσείς is also the plural of εσύ, so a question put to a whole shop or hotel (Έχετε ελεύθερα δωμάτια;) does not change. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: dumneavoastră
notes: The base rows: dumneavoastră with the second-person plural verb and imperative (puteți, vorbiți, opriți), vă and vă rog, as to any adult stranger.

label: tu
notes: tu with the second-person singular verb and imperative (poți, vorbește, oprește), îți and te rog, and the greetings bună and pa, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller; voi, its plural, takes the same verb as dumneavoastră, so a question put to a whole shop or hotel (Aveți camere libere?) does not change. The intermediate dumneata is not used. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: Ön
notes: The base rows: Ön with the third-person verb and imperative (tudna, beszél, beszéljen, álljon meg) and the courtesy formula kérem, as to any adult stranger; Önök, its plural, with the third-person plural (szobájuk, küldjenek).

label: te
notes: te with the second-person singular verb and imperative (tudnál, beszélsz, beszélj, állj meg), kérlek and szia, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller; ti, its plural, with the second-person plural (szobátok, küldjetek) where the base puts a question to a whole hotel or office. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: شما
notes: The base rows: شما with the second-person plural verb and imperative (می‌توانید, بنویسید, نگه دارید) and the enclitic ـتان, as to any adult stranger.

label: تو
notes: تو with the second-person singular verb and imperative (می‌توانی, بنویس, نگه دار) and the enclitic ـت, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller; شما is also the plural of تو, so a question put to a whole shop or hotel (اتاقِ خالی دارید؟) does not change. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.

label: Anda
notes: The base rows: Anda where a pronoun is needed, the address KBBI gives as not marking rank, standing or age, and the time-of-day greeting selamat siang, as to any adult stranger; most rows drop the pronoun (Bisa bantu saya?, Tolong ...) and read the same in both registers.

label: kamu
notes: kamu and its clitic -mu (bantuanmu), and the colloquial greetings hai and dah, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller; only the few rows that name the listener change. The speaker stays saya, which KBBI gives for ordinary as well as formal speech. e.g. hitchhiking.where-are-you-going.

label: anda
notes: The base rows: anda where a pronoun is needed, the second person Kamus Dewan gives as not marking rank, standing or age, as to any adult stranger; most rows drop the pronoun (Boleh bantu saya?, Tolong ...) and read the same in both registers.

label: awak
notes: awak, the conversational second person said to an equal (Kamus Pelajar: bp, and not to elders), to a friend or a fellow traveller; only the few rows that name the listener change. e.g. hitchhiking.where-are-you-going.

label: আপনি
notes: The base rows: আপনি with the polite verb (পারেন, দেবেন), its imperative (বলুন, দিন, থামুন, and the future দেবেন না for a prohibition) and আপনার, as to any adult stranger.

label: তুমি
notes: তুমি with the familiar verb (পারো, দেবে), its imperative (বলো, দাও, থামো, and the future দিয়ো না, কোরো না for a prohibition) and তোমার, to a child, a friend or a fellow traveller; the intimate তুই is never used. e.g. taxi.please-stop-here.
